# Marcus Vallance

> Marcus Vallance (also published as Marcus Valance) is a British portrait photographer. He began photographing in the refugee camps of Greece in 2015 and has since worked in camps and communities around the world. His photographs have been published internationally and exhibited in London, Milan, Madrid and Amsterdam. He is available for portrait commissions in the UK and abroad.

## About
Marcus Vallance picked up a camera in the winter of 2015 on the Greek island of Kos, where he had gone to volunteer as refugees came ashore from Turkey. He followed the route north through Greece to the Macedonian border and the camp at Idomeni. He has since photographed Syrian families in Jordan and Lebanon and the Rohingya in Bangladesh, among many other places. His work is syndicated through Getty Images and SOPA Images. His photograph "Boy Carrying a Bag of Grain" (Kutupalong refugee camp, Bangladesh) was chosen as a photograph of the week by The Guardian, and "Child at a Window" (Kutupalong refugee camp, Bangladesh) was shortlisted for best image in the documentary category at the British Photography Awards. His series "Hope", portraits of Rohingya children, was released as a limited collection with a quarter of the proceeds going to the Malala Fund. He was the sole exhibitor at the 2020 British Photography Awards at The Savoy, London. Alongside humanitarian work he photographs musicians, artists and brands.

Note on spelling: earlier press, agency and gallery credits use the spelling "Marcus Valance". Both refer to the same photographer.

## The collection (55 works)
- 01. Portrait of a Maasai, Zanzibar, Tanzania: profile of a man in a red checked shuka against the sea at sunset.
- 02. Playing Games, Tanzania: four men on a bench outside a whitewashed building, playing a board game.
- 03. Boy Carrying a Bag of Grain, Kutupalong Refugee Camp, Bangladesh: a laughing boy with wet hair balancing a bag of grain on his head, looking up. Photograph of the week, The Guardian.
- 04. Child at a Window, Kutupalong Refugee Camp, Bangladesh: a small child looking out through the bamboo frame of a window cut in an orange tarpaulin shelter. Shortlisted, Documentary, British Photography Awards.
- 05. Shivula, Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh: Shivula, a shallow-water fisherman, in a woven conical hat with a basket on his back.
- 06. Portrait of a Man, Bangladesh: an elderly man with a henna-dyed beard and white cap.
- 07. Portrait of a Girl, Tamale, Ghana: a girl with tribal marks on her cheeks, in a white headscarf, leaning on a railing in front of a yellow wall near Tamale.
- 08. Portrait of a Girl, Sindos Refugee Camp, Thessaloniki, Greece: a young girl with curly hair in a grey top embroidered with red flowers, standing in front of a tent inside a warehouse camp.
- 09. Aisha Bakary, Zanzibar, Tanzania: Zanzibari DJ and producer Aisha Bakary, known as the Hijab DJ, in a black headscarf and oversized tinted glasses, chin on her hand.
- 10. Portrait of a Boy, EKO Camp, Greece: an Afghan boy hanging from the door of a red and yellow caravan, pulling a face, in EKO refugee camp in northern Greece near the Macedonian border, July 2016.

## Questions
- Where is Marcus Vallance based? Marcus Vallance is based in Taunton, Somerset, and takes on portrait commissions across the UK and abroad.
- What kind of portraits does Marcus photograph? Editorial, press and album portraits, brand campaigns and private sittings. His work is made on location rather than in a studio: in refugee camps, on stage, on the street and in the places people live and work.
- Does Marcus travel for commissions? Yes. He has photographed in Greece, Lebanon, Bangladesh, Zanzibar, Nepal, Ghana, Colombia, Italy and across the UK, and is happy to travel for the right project.
- How much does a portrait commission cost? Every commission is priced to the job. Tell Marcus who, where and when, and he will come back with an approach and a quote.
- Does Marcus photograph musicians and artists? Yes. Musicians he has photographed include Tim Wheeler of Ash, Gary Stringer of Reef and Matt Cardle, on stage and off, for press, artwork and campaigns.
- Can I license one of these photographs? Yes. All photographs on this site can be licensed for editorial or commercial use. Get in touch and include the photograph's title or plate number. His work is also syndicated through Getty Images and SOPA Images.

## Commissions
Editorial, press and album portraits, brand campaigns and private sittings. Contact: https://marcusvallance.co.uk/contact or studio@marcusvallance.co.uk. Instagram: @marcusvallancephotography.
